notes: What the rig does with each cron a tracked Worker config declares (docs/RIG.md, Loonext in rig mode). Nothing fires a cron on a timer: an agent fires one on demand (rig cron) through /cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled; scripts/check-rig-crons.mjs fails when a config and this file disagree, and `--ref <ref>` checks another ref's configs against it.

run: the rig can fire it on demand. run-expect-refusal: the rig can fire it on demand, and when the named job has the work described in `when`, it reaches an account-wide Telnyx endpoint that rig mode refuses before any request leaves (apps/api/src/environments/policy.ts). skip: never fire it. Another Worker's cron (the edge's, the guard's) is always a skip, since the rig fires only the API's. A skip is never fired, so it raises nothing and needs nothing explained.

Refusals are listed for every code path that can reach one, not only for what today's seed exercises: a refusal that never happens costs nothing, and one that is missing is an unexplained exception in R00.

A refusal's outcome says what PostHog receives. job-fails: the job lets the TelnyxApiError out and runScheduledJobs reports it as an exception carrying the cron and the job; a job that collects its failures into an AggregateError (poll-registrations, poll-port-requests and grace-and-release do, and the release's own inside grace's) has each failure in it reported on its own, the same way. captured: the job catches it at caught_in and reports it as its own exception; follow_on_events lists what the job raises next because of it.

defects: events that mean the rig's seed or a scenario's setup is wrong, with the cause. Nothing suppresses them; R00 reports them with that cause instead of as unexplained. rigd reports the first defect that matches, so no two may match one event: `message starts` reads the event's own text, which for a cron's failure is the cron's AggregateError, so it tells an exception a job captured from the same exception inside a cron's failure.

A guard refusal (a 403 from the guard rather than the app) reaches the app as a TelnyxApiError with no code, which the app treats as a real Telnyx failure. None is expected: each one the crons can provoke is a defect.

Every cron here first asks rig_database_posture(): until the rig's database reports rig mode it throws `rig cron not run: ...`. That is an infrastructure fault for R00 to report, not an expected event, so no entry suppresses it.

refusal_match.why: The app sets no fingerprint on a refusal, so PostHog groups it by exception; its message is `Telnyx 403 on <METHOD> <path> [codes rig_endpoint_refused] ...`. A job-fails refusal arrives as an exception whose `cron` names the cron that ran it: suppress it only when every exception in it that is not an AggregateError matches a job-fails refusal listed for that cron, since anything else in it is a real failure. A captured refusal arrives as its own TelnyxApiError exception, raised while that cron runs: suppress it when the message has this text and one of the refusal's paths.

crons.note: Database scans plus pushes and texts through the guard. Scheduled sends pass the outbound destination gate, which refuses a destination outside the partition with rig_destination_refused before any request leaves. S05 and S25 depend on this cron.

Webhook replay, send recovery and outbound webhooks, which rig mode delivers to the robot sink or nowhere. Calendar sync has no connection to work on (X22). The edge relays no 10DLC or porting event, so the replay never reaches a refused endpoint.

reconcile-numbers lists the account's numbers through the guard and acts only on its own billing group. A group number with no phone_numbers row is flagged once per run, or, when its customer_reference names a settled workspace with nothing provisioning, DELETEd (provisioning.ts reconcileNumbers). The seed gives every standing number an active row, ROBOT-1, ROBOT-2 and STRANGER-1 under the Robot workspace (scripts/rig/tenants.mjs), so the sweep knows all eight.

refusals.when: an approved campaign row with a telnyx_id and no deactivated_at has an active number whose numberAssignments entry is neither added nor pending. Each run marks the number failed and the next run clears failed entries and tries again, so this is one event per such number each time the cron is fired: the US-number fallback's seeded registration must record every QA-W number as added, or carry no telnyx_id.

a text_enablement_orders row is pending, action-required or in-progress with fewer than 5 attempts. Each run spends one attempt per such order and raises one event for it, so an order raises at most 5.

follow_on_events.why: The fifth refused attempt marks the order failed and says so once; nothing polls a failed order.

defects.match: message starts "reconcile: a Telnyx number is unknown to phone_numbers"
defects.means: A number in the rig's group has no live phone_numbers row. The seed writes one for every standing number, so either a row was released or lost since the last seed (run rig seed), or the group holds a number that is not a standing one and no workspace bought. One warning per number per run, 96 a day each.

defects.match: TelnyxApiError "Telnyx 403 on DELETE /v2/phone_numbers/" with no [codes ...], tag job=job:reconcile-numbers
defects.means: reconcile-numbers tried to reclaim a group number that has no phone_numbers row and whose customer_reference names a settled seeded workspace, and the guard refused it because it is a standing number. Only the guard's standing-number rule stood between the sweep and the number: give the number a row or clear its customer_reference.

reconcile-voice-enablement tried to bind the voice app onto an active number whose row says its voice is off, and the guard refused it (provisioning.number_standing) because it is a standing number. Only the guard's standing-number rule kept a robot number off the voice app. The seed must write every number's row with voice_enabled on and the connection its role is on (scripts/rig/seed.mjs); run rig seed, or deploy, which reseeds a row with the flag off.

defects.match: level warning, message starts "voice enablement reconcile: "
defects.means: The same refusal, counted: the voice reconcile left numbers unbound at the end of a run. See the PATCH /v2/phone_numbers/ defect above for the cause.

defects.match: level warning, message starts "reconcile: reclaimed an orphaned Telnyx number"
defects.means: The same reclaim got through and a number in the rig's group was deleted. If it was a standing number, the guard's standing-number rule failed: critical.

crons.note: Usage goes to Stripe's shared test mode, which S01's meter check reads. sweep-stale-calls hangs up a runaway leg through the guard's leg-command class. telnyx-spend-gauges reads production's Telnyx spend limits and cost ledger in production only: productionWatchRefusal stops it in rig mode before any request, so it logs that it was skipped and returns.
Email only, through the guard's Resend path; it calls no 10DLC endpoint.
Calls the public Nominatim service, which has no seam and is not on the rig's DNS block list. It only ever sees seeded synthetic addresses, once each, at one request a second, and caches the answer.
As the contact geocoder: public Nominatim, seeded synthetic addresses only.
Database read plus one warning email per crew per day; S26 judges its 80% alert.

No job but the registration poller makes a Telnyx request. telnyx-capacity-gauge prices production's ring audience against the account's concurrent call limit in production only: productionWatchRefusal stops it in rig mode before any read, so it logs that it was skipped and returns. aup-signals sends one event per seeded workspace that texted, an event rather than an exception.

refusals.when: a brand or campaign row with a telnyx_id and no deactivated_at is submitted, pending, approved or suspended (each is polled), or an approved brand's campaign is a draft or deactivated (it is submitted). An approved campaign is also read a second time, for its content migration.
as retry-campaign-assignments on the */15 cron, which this job also runs once a day

crons.note: The portability check and the document upload are reached only from the porting routes, never from this job.

refusals.when: a port_requests row with a Telnyx order id is not ported or cancelled, or is voice-ported with messaging still pending: the poll's read of the order is refused

a draft port_requests row is due a resume, with no order yet (the saga creates one) or with an order and both documents (it is confirmed). The refusal is written to the row's rejection_reason and raised as its own event, once per such row per day.

crons.note: S29 fires this after backdating a workspace's cancellation. The release deletes every number that workspace holds (provisioning.ts releaseCompanyNumbers), so S29's workspace must hold no standing number: QA-C as RIG.md 3.3 lists it holds DEV-C1. See defects.

refusals.when: a workspace past its grace period still has an active 10DLC campaign to deactivate, or holds a hosted (text-enabled) number whose enablement order is not cancelled: releasing it deletes the hosted number, or the order while it is not completed

defects.match: TelnyxApiError "Telnyx 403 on DELETE /v2/phone_numbers/" with no [codes ...], tag job=job:grace-and-release
defects.means: The grace job tried to release a standing number and the guard refused it: S29 backdated a workspace that holds one. The job fails before it deactivates the workspace's campaign, and S29 cannot pass. Only the guard's standing-number rule kept the number. S29 needs a workspace whose only number is one bought for the run.

crons.note: Re-mirrors subscriptions from Stripe's shared test mode.

Reads /v2/messaging_optouts filtered by each workspace's own messaging profile, which the guard's read class allows. It keeps going past a workspace whose list cannot be read, reporting each one as its own exception.
Retention and purge against the local database and storage; the notices are email through the guard.
Asks the call Durable Object to send its heartbeat, an event rather than an exception, so nothing here needs explaining.

Monthly recap email to every active seeded workspace. The guard sends only to Resend's test addresses, and every member the seed creates has one (memberEmail in scripts/rig/tenants.mjs, pinned by tools/rig/test/seed.test.mjs).

crons.reason: loonext-rig-edge runs on Cloudflare, never on the rig box: its mail self-test and uplink housekeeping fire there on Cloudflare's clock, so the rig has nothing to fire.

The guard's weekly Telnyx key inventory, a Cloudflare cron on loonext-telnyx-guard that the rig box never fires. It reports to production's PostHog as ["ops","telnyx-key-inventory"], never to the rig's.

The guard's hourly upkeep on Cloudflare (expired legs, the robot mailbox's arrival deadline, the first order's read-back, the balance sample and the monthly cap), which the rig box never fires. What it raises goes to production's PostHog under the guard's own keys (telnyx-guard-order-group, telnyx-balance-low, telnyx-guard-detach), never to the rig's.
